title: Using ChatGPT in HCI Research—A Trioethnography

bias_targets.methodology: Autoethnographic observation of account creation friction, comparing the system's repeated rejection of a Global South (Bangladesh) phone number as 'suspicious' versus the immediate acceptance of a Global North (UK) phone number.

Qualitative observation of content moderation policies, comparing the system's strict flagging of Western cultural transgressions (like slavery and discrimination) against its failure to flag offensive caste-based terms (e.g., 'Chamar') and statements asserting caste supremacy.

Prompting the model to generate short biographies of various world leaders and qualitatively comparing the inclusion of critiques for Global South/Eastern leaders (e.g., Modi, Hasina, Xi Jinping) versus the absence of criticism for Western leaders (e.g., Biden).

Translating sentences with gender-neutral pronouns from a local language into English to observe if the model assigns stereotypical gender pronouns to specific tasks (e.g., 'He earns money' vs. 'She cooks').

Evaluating the model's responses to queries about marginalized labor (e.g., digital sex work, domestic worker cooperatives), observing false legal classifications and a systemic preference for recommending exploitative, capitalist gig-economy structures over worker-owned models.
